/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 156: Couldn't resolve reference to property definition 'ARINC653::HM_Errors'.: The target thread type uses ARINC653 property names and enumeration literals, but the defining property set is not resolved in the model scope. -> Add or correct the package-level `with ARINC653;` dependency so `ARINC653::HM_Errors` and its listed literals resolve; do not change the AGREE annex for this issue.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 157: Couldn't resolve reference to property definition 'ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions'.: The target thread type uses a second ARINC653 property whose definition and enumeration literals are also unresolved in the current model scope. -> Use the same package-level dependency repair so `ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions` and its listed literals resolve; preserve the existing property clause text if the import alone fixes it.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 159: left and right sides of binary expression '<=' are of type '<error>' and 'int', but must be of the same type: `temp` is visible in the annex, but its owner feature does not currently resolve to a typed AGREE numeric expression, so the assumption cannot type-check. -> Keep the existing assumption text and repair the owner feature declaration for `temp` so it resolves to a valid AGREE integer-typed input; only if that cannot be done with an existing model type should the assumption be removed as a last resort.

/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 156: Couldn't resolve reference to property definition 'ARINC653::HM_Errors'.: The enclosing AADL package does not make the `ARINC653` property set visible, so existing `ARINC653::...` property associations and their literals are unresolved across the model. -> Add or correct the package-level `with ARINC653;` import so the existing `ARINC653::HM_Errors`, `ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions`, `ARINC653::Partition_Slots`, `ARINC653::Slots_Allocation`, `ARINC653::HM_Module_Recovery_Actions`, and related literals resolve without changing the AGREE annex.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 159: named thing must be an expression with a type: `temp` is not resolving to a typed numeric AGREE input in `commandboard_receiveinput_thread`, so both comparisons see `<error>` on the left side. -> Fix only the existing `temp` feature declaration so it references the model's valid integer data classifier, then keep the assumption text exactly `temp >= 0 and temp <= 100`.

/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | lines 152, 156, 157: unresolved property associations around the target owner (`Source_Stack_Size`, `ARINC653::HM_Errors`, `ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions`): The target thread type sits in an unresolved AADL owner context because existing property-set references are not currently resolvable, which can cascade into AGREE typing failures in the annex below. -> Repair property-set visibility for the already-referenced property associations in and above `commandboard_receiveinput_thread` instead of rewriting the AGREE contract; use existing property-set names already present in the model.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 159: `temp >= 0 and temp <= 100` reports `temp` as `<error>` and not a typed expression: The assumption text itself uses only the visible symbol `temp` and integer literals, so the AGREE failure is most likely a cascading type-resolution problem from the surrounding unresolved model context rather than a bad range expression. -> Keep the assume clause text unchanged after the owner/model resolution fix; only if `temp` still remains untyped, edit only `temp`'s declaration to use an already-existing resolvable integer data classifier without changing the assumption expression.

/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 159: named thing must be an expression with a type: The AGREE assume clause is syntactically valid, but `temp` is not resolving to a typed AGREE numeric expression in `commandboard_receiveinput_thread`, so both comparisons type-check as `<error>`. -> In the owner feature declaration, replace the unresolved `integer` classifier on `temp` with the model's resolvable integer data classifier, and leave `assume "temp bounded": temp >= 0 and temp <= 100;` unchanged.

/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 156: Couldn't resolve reference to property definition 'ARINC653::HM_Errors'.: The target thread type contains an unresolved ARINC653 property association that is outside the AGREE contract and causes owner-level validation failure. -> Delete the `ARINC653::HM_Errors => (Deadline_Miss, Application_Error, Numeric_Error, Illegal_Request);` association from `commandboard_receiveinput_thread`.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 157: Couldn't resolve reference to property definition 'ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions'.: The target thread type contains a second unresolved ARINC653 property association with unresolved enumeration literals, again outside the AGREE contract. -> Delete the `ARINC653::HM_Process_Recovery_Actions => (Process_Restart, Process_Stop, Process_Stop, Process_Stop);` association from `commandboard_receiveinput_thread`.
/CaseProject/modified_model.aadl | line 159: named thing must be an expression with a type; left and right sides of `>=` and `<=` are of type `<error>` and `int`.: The annex assumption itself matches the requirement, but `temp` is not resolving as a typed numeric feature in the owner declaration, so AGREE cannot type-check the comparison. -> Repair the `temp` feature declaration in `commandboard_receiveinput_thread` so it uses a resolvable integer data type already available to the model, and keep the existing assumption text unchanged.
